transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-10
Time: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Mateo Ruiz (Redwood), Liam O'Connor (Solarflare), Marisol Vega (Solarflare), Akira Saito (Solarflare), Nadia Chen (Solarflare)

Summary:
Quick technical gate review for the joint marketplace listing and hybrid deployment pattern. Focus areas: packaging (kustomize vs helm), VPC connectivity for private deployments, KMS/HSM key flow for model keys, autoscale / burst on dedicated pools, and a short plan for running a quantized perf run to validate latency and cost.

Topics:
- Packaging and manifest patterns for Marketplace listing
- Network connectivity / private registry and VPC peering
- Security: KMS, cert rotation, audit logs
- Runtime perf: quantization, batching, KV cache behavior
- Rollout gates and acceptance criteria for joint solution

Action items (captured above)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — I see Liam, Marisol, Akira, Nadia from Solarflare and then Priya and Mateo from our side. Uh, we'll keep this pretty focused, we have about 50 minutes.

[00:22] Liam O'Connor: Yep hi, thanks Jordan. We wanted to make sure the marketplace listing doesn't, erm, create extra ops work for us and that the hybrid variant — the VPC/private deployment — matches our compliance checklist.

[00:35] Priya Patel: Totally, that's the intention. We'll walk through two packaging options — a helm chart with marketplace hooks and a kustomize overlay for private installs — and then dive into the KMS and cert rotation story.

[01:10] Marisol Vega: Quick note, our PM priority is: predictable rollout, so we can preview in staging and then flip to production. Also, we have an internal SLA for 99.9 for inference latency p95 for the demo tenant.

[01:40] Mateo Ruiz: Got it. To frame expectations — Redwood's marketplace artifact can support both a hosted listing (redirects to hosted API) and a hybrid listing which includes a cloud-init style bundle for private deploy. There are a few options for packaging: single-tenant helm, or a chart + kustomize overlays. Each has tradeoffs for patching and customer-managed registry.

[02:15] Akira Saito: For the hybrid we need to know the exact container images we have to whitelist in our airgap pipeline, and a mechanism for image signature verification. Can Redwood sign images, or do we need to bring them?

[02:35] Priya Patel: We can provide signed images via our registry and give attestation metadata. For private/on-prem we also support bringing-your-own-image (BYOI) — in that case we'd supply a reference manifest and a digest you can pin.

[03:05] Nadia Chen: From security: KMS integration is important. Do you support customer-managed keys (CMK) in both hosted and private modes? And how is key rotation handled without causing model serving disruption?

[03:30] Jordan Kim: Short answer: yes we support CMKs for private deployments, and for hosted we have a managed KMS but we offer Bring-Your-KMS for enterprise plans. Rotation is done via a staged key swap — SEs, correct me if I mess this up — we keep a short-lived decryption envelope so the runtime can switch to the new key without restarting long-lived processes.

[03:55] Priya Patel: Right, the runtime uses envelope encryption. We rewrap the model encryption key under the new CMK, then signal the serving process to refresh keys and reload the model seamlessly. There is a small cache-eviction window for in-flight KV cache, but we've seen under 30s of jitter in tests.

[04:25] Liam O'Connor: Thirty seconds is acceptable, but we need logs and audit events around the rotation. Also, Nadia wants assurance about HSM-backed ops.

[04:45] Nadia Chen: Yes we will need audit trails, and proof that keys are HSM-protected. Can that be shown in a SOC2 artifact or some integration test?

[05:05] Jordan Kim: We can share SOC2 summary and HSM attestation redacted artifacts. I'll add that as an action item.

[05:25] Marisol Vega: Great. Switching to perf, we want to validate a quantized 4-bit variant for cost savings. How does Redwood recommend quantization profiles and what are the expected latency tradeoffs?

[05:50] Priya Patel: We recommend two profiles: latency-optimized (per-token kernel selection, minimum batch size 1, slightly larger memory footprint) and cost-optimized (aggressive quantization + batching). For 4-bit, typical p95 increases by ~5-15% but cost per token drops by 30-45% depending on sequence length and KV cache hit rate.

[06:25] Akira Saito: Can we run a short benchmark against your dedicated pool with our sample prompts? We need to see tail latency under 256-token prompts.

[06:40] Mateo Ruiz: Yes, we can provision a small dedicated run; we'll need a representative workload, docker registry read, and a prom endpoint we can scrape for traces. Priya will own the perf template.

[07:00] Liam O'Connor: Also, our traffic is bursty — daily peaks for 10 minutes where throughput is 5x baseline. How do we handle burst capacity for dedicated pools so the marketplace listing won't fail?

[07:20] Priya Patel: Redwood Dedicated supports burst capacity and autoscale policies. For marketplace hybrid listing we can declare an optional burst contract that Solarflare can subscribe to. Alternatively, for the private variant you can configure local autoscaler and fallback routing to hosted if you permit that in your policy.

[07:55] Marisol Vega: Fallback to hosted is a political decision; we may not be able to allow hosting of sensitive data.

[08:10] Jordan Kim: Understood. We'll treat fallback as opt-in but it's useful to plan so you have capacity buffers.

[08:30] Akira Saito: Network: for VPC peering, what's the minimum firewall/port open list? We need specifics to run with our network team and firewall reviewers.

[08:45] Priya Patel: We'll share a minimal manifest. Generally we need outbound HTTPS to Redwood control plane on 443, and gRPC ports for the runtime inter-node comms if you choose a dedicated cluster. For private on-prem, we support a direct peering mode or transit mode — peering is straightforward, transit uses a connector. I'll attach a sample security group in the follow-up.

[09:20] Nadia Chen: We also need to confirm that audit logs include per-request metadata, token counts, and model version identifiers.

[09:35] Mateo Ruiz: Yes, the Console emits token-level cost breakdowns and model-version tags. For private deployments you can send logs to your SIEM, or we can push to a forwarder.

[10:00] Liam O'Connor: Ok good. A few practical questions about the marketplace listing UX: will our team be able to opt for a managed listing where Redwood handles billing, or do we want to surface a connector so we can bill directly?

[10:20] Jordan Kim: Two models: Redwood-managed billing (simpler) or vendor-billed listing — in which case we surface meter events and a metering API you call. Both are supported; we'll include an appendix in the listing docs.

[10:45] Marisol Vega: For vendor-billed we need metering granularity per-route and per-tenant. Is that fine?

[10:55] Priya Patel: Yes, per-route token and embedding meters are available. We'll provide sample CSV/BigQuery export formats.

[11:15] Akira Saito: Back to packaging — our infra team prefers kustomize because we have an airgap toolchain that consumes overlays. Do you have a canonical kustomize overlay setup for the hybrid listing?

[11:35] Mateo Ruiz: We do. Typically the overlay will patch image digests, set registry credentials secrets, and toggle the KMS provider. We also provide an example helm hook for preflight checks. The overlay + helm combo is common when customers want both reproducible installs and Helm lifecycle hooks.

[12:05] Liam O'Connor: Can you demo the kustomize overlay quickly? Even a short walkthrough would help.

[12:15] Priya Patel: Sure, give me a minute to pull up the snippet.

[12:45] Priya Patel: [screen share sounds like] So here's a base deployment with a kustomization.yaml and we patch the config map to point to your registry. The patch includes a secretRef for registry creds. Also we include an optional post-install hook that runs a small smoke test.

[13:30] Marisol Vega: The smoke test should validate model load and a smoke inference call. Can we make it return a 200 and a token count?

[13:50] Priya Patel: Yes, the smoke hook invokes the /health and /infer endpoints, asserts latency < 500ms on a short prompt and returns token count. We can parametrize thresholds.

[14:15] Akira Saito: On cert rotation: is there an operator that rotates serving certs, or do we rely on k8s cert-manager? We need the pattern for zero-downtime cert refresh.

[14:35] Mateo Ruiz: We integrate with cert-manager. The operator will update the secret and we watch for secret changes to hot-reload certs. That refresh is done without pod restarts as long as the runtime process supports SIGHUP-style reconfigure. We built that in.

[15:05] Nadia Chen: Auditing note: we need to keep a 1-year trail of key events. Is that configurable?

[15:20] Jordan Kim: Yes log retention can be set. For private deployments you can forward to your SIEM for long-term retention, otherwise we provide configurable retention tiers.

[15:40] Liam O'Connor: Great. A small nit: our compliance team will want to run a short pen test on the listing preflight. How long does Redwood need to approve penetration testing?

[15:55] Priya Patel: For hosted it usually takes 2-3 weeks for coordination. For private/on-prem it's your environment so you can run it, we just ask for a heads-up and a test window to ensure no surprise throttles.

[16:15] Marisol Vega: Ok, moving to acceptance gates: we propose the following gates — packaging validated (kustomize/helm), perf validated on quantized profile, security artifacts provided, and billing/metering contract agreed. Anything missing?

[16:35] Jordan Kim: That sounds good. I'd add operational runbook handoff and backup/restore validation as a final gate.

[16:50] Akira Saito: Backup/restore for model artifacts is important — we need a validated checksum process and a tested restore within our DR windows. Can we include a small restore test in the benchmark run?

[17:05] Mateo Ruiz: Absolutely. We can script a model export/restore and time the operation. We'll include that in the perf template.

[17:30] Liam O'Connor: On the benchmark itself, question about telemetry — can we stream traces to our Jaeger instance?

[17:45] Priya Patel: Yes, we can forward traces or provide OTLP exporters. We'll collect p95, p99, token breakdowns, and KV cache hit rates.

[18:10] Marisol Vega: One more question on KV cache: in a distributed setup, do you maintain a shared KV or a local per-node KV? We worry about warm-up times after scale events.

[18:30] Priya Patel: The runtime uses a local KV cache per serving process with a coordinated warm-up and prefill mechanism. For heavy scale events we have a pre-warm mode where the controller pulls top prefixes to nodes prior to traffic shift. That reduces cold-start tails.

[18:55] Akira Saito: That pre-warm sounds promising, what's required from our side to trigger pre-warm?

[19:05] Mateo Ruiz: You can annotate the deployment with a prewarm policy, or for the marketplace we can include it as a default in the overlay. It needs allowed egress for the prefetch and a small helper job.

[19:30] Liam O'Connor: Regarding telemetry again — we will need an approval from finance to move to vendor-billed. Is there a rough timeline for listing to go live once we sign a vendor billing contract?

[19:45] Jordan Kim: From contract to live listing typically 3-4 weeks if packaging and security checks move quickly. Perf and benchmark can run in parallel.

[20:05] Marisol Vega: Ok that's reasonable. Let's lock on dates: we aim to get the benchmark run done by 2027-11-24 and a draft listing manifest by 2027-11-17.

[20:25] Jordan Kim: Noted; I'll put those in the action items.

[20:45] Nadia Chen: A practical ask — please include a short checklist for our auditors: what artifacts we'll get, SSO/SAML config, and a sample KMS policy.

[21:05] Priya Patel: We'll add an auditor checklist to the marketplace docs and include SSO/SCIM examples for SAML.

[21:25] Liam O'Connor: Perfect. Any blockers we foresee on our side?

[21:35] Marisol Vega: Registry access and a definitive list of sample prompts for perf. We'll deliver both this week.

[21:50] Akira Saito: Also we might need a short compatibility note on our airgap pipeline — the chart needs to be templatable without internet access.

[22:05] Mateo Ruiz: We support airgap manifests; we'll provide a tarball and a checksum-signed manifest.

[22:25] Jordan Kim: Great. We're nearing the top of the hour — any final clarifying Qs?

[22:35] Nadia Chen: Just one: for the HSM proof, is redacted attestation sufficient for us to sign off internally?

[22:50] Jordan Kim: Usually yes, but we can escalate to legal if you need the full attestation under an NDA.

[23:05] Marisol Vega: That might be necessary, we'll flag it.

[23:20] Jordan Kim: Alright, quick recap and next steps: Jordan to send packaging examples and marketplace checklist by 11/17; Priya to run perf template and coordinate dedicated run by 11/18; Solarflare to provide workload and registry access by 11/15; Nadia to share compliance artifact requests by 11/19. We'll also schedule the benchmark run for week of 11/22 if that works.

[23:50] Liam O'Connor: Works for us. Thanks everyone.

[24:00] Jordan Kim: Thanks all — we'll follow up over email and attach the kustomize/helm snippets. End call.

Notes on transcription: occasional filler words and some product names mis-transcribed (e.g., 'KV cache' rendered as 'K V cache' in spots), speaker turn boundaries imperfect in a few overlaps.
